text:
riya: quick thought — our per-tenant region-weight map feels brittle when probe signals flip. thinking about moving to a signal-driven reconciliation loop that emits soft deltas instead of hard overwrites. want quick sanity check on tradeoffs.

alex: +1 to soft deltas. do you mean stream deltas from probes into a reconcilier that smooths them before applying?

riya: yeah — probes -> aggregator -> reconciler. reconciler would emit 'apply' events that mutate tenant routing state, with TTLs. avoids thrashing when probes are noisy.

samir: watch out for coupling. if reconciler is stateful per-region we add another class of failover to test. is this a sidecar service or part of the policy engine?

riya: good call. leaning towards a small stateless reconciler + distributed cache for short-lived state (leases + monotonic change ids). that way the policy runtime stays simple and just subscribes to final deltas.

ingrid: how do we prevent a burst of deltas from oscillating runtime behavior? we already saw cost spikes when regions flip quickly. smoothing config should be tunable per-tenant.

alex: propose a two-layer smoothing: short-window EWMA + floor on change magnitude. i.e., ignore delta if weight change < 0.05 unless repeated N times. simple and cheap.

samir: operational concerns: cross-region reconciliation needs vector clocks or causal IDs so we don't regress on out-of-order signals. also need an explainability hook: given a routing decision, we should show which reconciler delta caused it.

riya: agree on explainability. idea: reconciler emits metadata blob with each apply event: {"source":"probe|manual|sim","delta":"+0.12","epoch":"167...","trace_id":"..."}. runtime attaches that to decision logs.

alex: minor nit — keep blobs small. prefer stringified tags rather than full nested JSON in the hot path. e.g., "src=probe;d=+0.12;eid=167". easier to index.

ingrid: testing plan: 1) sim harness with adversarial probe noise 2) canary reconciler + runtime in staging 3) metric-based rollback (we already have cost/latency SLOs).

riya: +1. also want a cheap offline simulation mode: feed historical probe time series and compute delta churn and expected cost impact. helps pick EWMA alpha and magnitude floor.

samir: what's the API between reconciler and runtime? pub/sub? HTTP push? I'd vote for a durable pubsub + per-tenant partition so we can replay in debug.

alex: agree pubsub. durable + ack semantics lets us rehydrate runtime after failover. runtime should also be able to request a full snapshot for a tenant on start.

riya: initial config sketch:
```
reconciler:
  smoothing:
    ewma_alpha: 0.2
    min_delta: 0.05
    repeat_threshold: 3
  snapshot_ttl: 60s
  publish_channel: "tenant-routing-deltas"
```

samir: looks reasonable. include max-rate-per-tenant to avoid noisy tenants dominating infra.

ingrid: also surface a health signal: reconciler_lag_seconds and delta_apply_rate. ops can alert if lag > X or apply_rate spikes.

ops-bot: deploy-ci: reconciler-service build succeeded (sha: d3f4a7).

riya: ok next steps: 1) I’ll spin up a sim with 3 workloads and noisy probes, tune EWMA 2) samir to prototype pubsub + snapshot API 3) alex to write explainability tag format and index plan 4) ingrid to draft staging canary checklist. will post RFC follow-up with perf numbers.

alex: sounds good. one more thought — we should keep a graceful degrade path where, if reconciler unreachable, runtime falls back to last-known snapshot + static bucketing to avoid complete outage.

riya: agreed. fallback semantics will be part of the RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
